MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 23, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on March 23, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on March 18, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING AGENDA MATTER

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that one matter arose after the agenda was posted and that
there is a need for the Council to take immediate action to consider to return to on-site City Council
Meetings due to the recent move from purple tier to red tier within Orange County. This item will
be discussed before Public Comments.

City Council Minutes  1  March 23, 2021
 Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum to declare that a matter
arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda and that the Council needs to take immediate action
regarding the return to on-site City Council Meetings due to the fact that the County is now in the
red tier and will soon be moving to the orange tier.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under
  Negotiation-Price and Terms.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the Council only addressed the real estate item and will
return after open session to address the other item, CS1, the voting rights case. As to the CS2
item, price and terms were discussed, the Council was advised and gave direction, but there was
reportable action.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize 2020 Orange County Sheriff’s Department Mission Viejo Employee of the
  Year Cody Eliason

  The Mayor recognized 2020 Orange County Sheriff's Department Mission Viejo Employee
  of the Year Cody Eliason.

City Council Minutes  2  March 23, 2021
 P2. Featured Business of the Month - Wineworks for Everyone and Dublin 4 Gastropub

  Presented proclamations to business owners Darren and Jean Coyle.

Late Agenda Item Added

  A. Return to On-Site City Council Meetings (Item added to the agenda)

  Mayor Kelley gave her report.

  Council Members voiced their opinions on returning to the Council Chamber for meetings.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to return to
  on-site Council Meetings starting April 13. with City Council only and to have staff prepare
  accommodations for the general public participation at a future meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  City Attorney Curley announced that when re-open to the general public that the Chamber
  will be limited capacity with seats marked for six-foot separation. There will be a section for
  Staff and escorts to show the public that they will enter through the back of the Chamber and
  exit through the door next to the big screen. He didn’t want the public to be surprised that we
  will not be at 100% capacity right away.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg reminded the Council that next week on March 31 at the joint
  meeting with the Planning Commission that it is a virtual meeting and has been noticed as
  such.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Judith Berman, M.V.: Announced that the deadline to apply for a Scholarship through the Mission
Viejo Activities Committee (MVAC) has been extended to April 2, 2021 at 2:00 p.m. Applicants
need to call the MVAC office to schedule an appointment if they wish to submit their application
in person. Information is on the MVAC website mvactivities.com.

Adi Mitchell, M.V., Cathy Allen, M.V., and Dave Breazeale, M.V.: stated that they are again a
beekeeping ordinance in Mission Viejo.

Joel Paget: Asked that that there be a police presence at the intersection of Marguerite Parkway
and Oso Parkway due to the amount of red-light violations. Expressed concerns that a fatal
accident could occur.

CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  3  March 23, 2021
 Item 11 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 9, 2021, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 26, 2021 in the Amount of $864,575.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated March 5, 2021 in the Amount of $2,652,804.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  National Association of State Procurement Officials (NASPO) ValuePoint Wireless
  Communication Services with Verizon Wireless

  Approved and authorized staff to sign the Local Government Request for NASPO Valuepoint
  Agreements and submit the request to the California Department of General Services;
  Approve and authorize the staff to sign the Participating Addendum to the NASPO ValuePoint
  Wireless Communication Services and Equipment Master Agreement Number MA152;
  Authorize staff to approve NASPO's future negotiated agreement following the existing
  expiration for August 11, 2024 or amended existing contract agreement.

5.  Routine Maintenance Contracts - Renewal and Bidding Cycles

  (1) Approved contract Group-1 renewals all of which have 1 (2)-year term available in
  accordance with the current contracts; (2) approved the contract extension offers in Group -2,
  which have no remaining renewable term available, for 1 additional (2)-year term; and (3)
  authorized staff to return to City Council with the individual contract awards and associated
  contract amounts.

6.  Contract Amendment for Electrical Related Services at City Facilities

  Approved third amendment for David Electric for electrical related services and repairs at city
  facilities for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00.

7.  Contract Amendment for Air Conditioning Related Services at City Facilities

City Council Minutes  4  March 23, 2021
   Approved first amendment for South Coast Mechanical for HVAC related services and repairs
  at City Hall and the Library for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not
  to exceed $30,000.00.

8.  Contract Amendment for Fire Protection Related Services at City Facilities

  Approved first amendment for Go Fire Protection Incorporated for fire protection related
  services and repairs at city facilities for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an
  amount not to exceed $20,000.00.

9.  Contract Amendment for Pool Maintenance Related Services at City Recreation Centers

  Approved first amendment for 1st Choice Pool & Spa Solutions for pool maintenance related
  services and repairs at city recreation centers for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021
  in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00.

10. Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 21-06 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

12. Annual Park and Facility Hardscape Construction Improvement Contract - S. Parker
  Engineering, Inc.

  (1) Approved Seventh Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with S. Parker
  Engineering, Inc for the subject services; and (2) authorized a Change Order to the existing
  Purchase Order for S. Parker Engineering, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $215,000.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

11.  Mutual Aid Agreement or the COVID-19 Vaccination Effort

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve and
  authorize the City Manager or designee to execute a Mutual Aid Agreement for the COVID-
  19 Vaccination Effort with the County of Orange, pertaining to mutual aid assistance provided
  under the Orange County Operational Area Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  5  March 23, 2021
 13.  Fiscal Year 2020/21 Budget Review

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 21-07 Amending the FY 2020/21 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley

15. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

16. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Wilberg spoke about the expansion of hours at the recreation and tennis centers along
with services at the Norman P. Community Center. He announced that the Library will be
reopening on April 6 in a phased approach with scheduled appointments. City Manager Wilberg
informed the Council that the Nadadores will be hosting a swim meet the weekend of April 8-11
that will involve lane closures on Marguerite due to NBC televising this event. The Nadadores
Dive Team plans to host two events in May for a high school regional dive meet and an AAU Dive
Meet. He announced that he has been working with the Pacific Symphony to hold their Annual
Gala on the Village Green and in addition they have been working with Keith Rattay to host smaller
concerts with limited attendance. Lastly, he announced that the Oso Creek Golf Course will be
closed next week for three days for the periodic aeration of the greens and some normal routine
maintenance.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Curley stated in addition to the ongoing issues with property acquisitions we have
been monitoring in conjunction with the League of California Cities new legislation that is being
proposed. He stated that there is some troubling legislation one is called “the right to housing” and
if it becomes law every city will be obligated to provide housing to anyone that needs it at the city’s
own cost, and if the city does not have housing of its own the city will be required to pay for hotel,
City Council Minutes  6  March 23, 2021
 room and board for up to three days per person. City Attorney Curley indicated that there a number
of Bills that take away local zoning control depending on where in the city the property may be, if
it is close to transportation within a half a mile every single-family lot could be converted up to at
10-unit apartment. If you are not within that distance lots could go to a 4-6-unit apartment. Single
family neighborhoods will lose the right to maintain single family residence. The State is trying to
respond to both the housing shortage and the climate crisis if your close to transportation there will
be less cars. Sacramento believes by overriding local zoning will cure the housing and climate
problems.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had no additional comments this evening.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated Cody Eliason on being named Mission Viejo Orange County
Sheriff Employee of the Year. Thanked our Sheriff Department for keeping out City safe. He
complimented City Staff on the great job they have been doing this past year.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs commented that he received via mail an advertisement for cannabis
delivery. He asked the City Attorney to write a letter to this company to inform them that they are
not allowed to distribute cannabis within the City. Secondly, he asked that Mayor Kelley
appointment two Council Members to an ad hoc committee for the Stein Mart negotiations. He
pointed out that when the Council does return to the Chamber I.T. needs to work on the echoing
situation. Lastly, stated that he is glad the marching band will return at Mission Viejo High School
during the football games.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum also congratulated Cody Eliason on being named Mission Viejo
Orange County Sheriff Employee of the Year. She encouraged residents to support our local
businesses.

Mayor Kelley

18. Consideration of Fee Waiver to Change the Street name from "Moor Avenue" to
  "Lobo Way" in the Address of Los Alisos Intermediate School

City Council Minutes  7  March 23, 2021
   Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to waive the City
  Application fee in the amount of $6,900 to change the street name and any installation fee for
  the replacement street signs.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Kelley touched on the beekeeping ordinance and voiced her opposition at the last meeting
citing concerns for safety of our residents and asked that staff to prepare a blog article for the
residents so that they may understand the ordinance. She mentioned the COVID 19 vaccinations
have been opened to a new group. Tier 1B is no open for education, food service, grocery and
agricultural workers, child care providers and emergency services. Those between ages 16-64 that
have underlying medical conditions as outlined by the State are also included. Mayor Kelley
reminded residents that they can register for the vaccine at the following websites: Othena.com,
myturn.ca.gov, cvs.com, and riteaid.com. She asked residents are having trouble registering to
reach out to city staff. Mayor Kelley reminded the public that Orange County and Saddleback
Church have been working on a virtual Job Fair on April 7 from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Lastly, she
stated that she is so happy that kids sports has returned.

The Mayor announced that the City Council will go back into Closed Session to discuss CS1.
The City Attorney announced that the City Council will discuss the remaining closed session item
regarding litigation dealing with the voting rights issue.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 8:30 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 9:10 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

Due to audio difficulties the City Attorney asked the City Clerk to announce that there was no
reportable action for CS1.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:16 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Wednesday March 31, at 6:00 p.m. for Joint Kick-off
Virtual Workshop of The City Council and Planning and Transportation Commission Housing
Element Update, 2021-2029 Planning Period.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

City Council Minutes  8  March 23, 2021
 Approved at the meeting of April 13, 2021

City Council Minutes  9  March 23, 2021
